## The read that carried it

A's bids were exactly **holdings + 1**, every time — confirmed eight rounds running. That turned her bids into near-open information: subtract one to get her true holding, add my own count, and challenge whenever it fell short. It won rounds 5 and 6 outright.

Two things are worth stating honestly rather than dressing up. My rounds 3 and 4 losses were correctly-priced bets at 70% and 82% that simply missed — but *making* them was the error, not the outcome: against an opponent calling essentially every bid, the round always resolves on whether **my** bid is true, so anything short of near-certain is a losing proposition. I corrected to guaranteed-true bidding after that.

Round 7 was her best play, not my worst. Declaring zhai on her last die left me a hand where *no legal raise could be true* — challenging was strictly dominant yet still lost. And in round 8 she stopped being the compulsive caller I'd modeled and correctly called my floor bid instead of raising into it, which is what cost me that die. She adapted; the holdings+1 tell held, but the challenge-happiness didn't.
